hints: Differentiate each term of $2y^2 + 3xy + x = x^2$ with respect to $x$, applying the chain rule to $2y^2$ and the product rule to $3xy$.
Collect all terms containing $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ on one side and factor out $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$.
walkthrough:
Differentiate each term of the equation $2y^2 + 3xy + x = x^2$ with respect to $x$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}[2y^2] = 4y\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$$
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}[3xy] = 3(1)y + 3x\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 3y + 3x\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$$
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}[x] = 1$$
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}[x^2] = 2x$$

Combine the derivatives into a single equation:
$$4y\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} + 3y + 3x\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} + 1 = 2x$$

Rearrange to collect all terms with $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ on the left-hand side:
$$4y\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} + 3x\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 2x - 3y - 1$$
$$(4y + 3x)\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 2x - 3y - 1$$

Divide both sides by $(4y + 3x)$ to obtain the required derivative:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{2x - 3y - 1}{4y + 3x}$$

ai_rubric.Implicit Differentiation: Differentiates $2y^2$ to $4y(dy/dx)$ (B1). Differentiates $3xy$ to $3y + 3x(dy/dx)$ (B1). Differentiates all terms and groups $dy/dx$ terms (M1). Obtains $(2x - 3y - 1)/(4y + 3x)$ (A1).

skill_tags: Finding Points from a Gradient Condition

hints: A tangent parallel to the $x$-axis has gradient $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 0$.
Set the numerator equal to zero: $2x - 3y - 1 = 0 \implies 2x = 3y + 1$.
Substitute into the original equation and examine the discriminant of the resulting quadratic.
walkthrough:
A tangent is parallel to the $x$-axis if and only if $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 0$, which requires the numerator to be zero (provided the denominator is non-zero):
$$2x - 3y - 1 = 0 \implies 2x = 3y + 1 \implies x = \dfrac{3y + 1}{2}$$

Substitute $x = \dfrac{3y + 1}{2}$ into the curve equation $2y^2 + 3xy + x = x^2$:
$$2y^2 + 3\left(\dfrac{3y + 1}{2}\right)y + \left(\dfrac{3y + 1}{2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{3y + 1}{2}\right)^2$$

Multiply every term by $4$ to clear all denominators:
$$4(2y^2) + 4\left(\dfrac{3y(3y + 1)}{2}\right) + 4\left(\dfrac{3y + 1}{2}\right) = 4\left(\dfrac{(3y + 1)^2}{4}\right)$$
$$8y^2 + 6y(3y + 1) + 2(3y + 1) = (3y + 1)^2$$

Subtract $9y^2 + 6y + 1$ from both sides to form a quadratic in standard form $Ay^2 + By + C = 0$:
$$(26 - 9)y^2 + (12 - 6)y + (2 - 1) = 0$$
$$17y^2 + 6y + 1 = 0$$

Calculate the discriminant $\Delta = B^2 - 4AC$ for this quadratic equation:
$$\Delta = 6^2 - 4(17)(1) = 36 - 68 = -32$$
Since $\Delta = -32 < 0$, the quadratic equation $17y^2 + 6y + 1 = 0$ has no real solutions for $y$.
Alternatively, expressing in terms of $x$ via $y = \dfrac{2x - 1}{3}$ gives $17x^2 - 8x + 2 = 0$ with discriminant $(-8)^2 - 4(17)(2) = 64 - 136 = -72 < 0$, also yielding no real solutions.
Therefore, there is no point on the curve where $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 0$, so the curve does not have any tangent parallel to the $x$-axis.

ai_rubric.Finding Points from a Gradient Condition: Equates numerator to zero to get $2x = 3y + 1$ and substitutes into curve equation (M1). Obtains quadratic in one variable, e.g. $17y^2 + 6y + 1 = 0$ or $17x^2 - 8x + 2 = 0$ (DM1). Uses negative discriminant ($-32$ or $-72$) to conclude no real roots (A1).
